chapter_title: Chương 37: 0037【Trà Sữa Cũng Đầy Vẻ Tiểu Tư Sản】

segments.title: Chương 37: 0037【Trà Sữa Cũng Đầy Vẻ Tiểu Tư Sản】
segments.content:
Suddenly handsome, Chen Guiliang swaggered out of the barbershop. "Let's go, I'll treat you to some bubble tea."

"Let me treat you instead. Last time we went to get the computer fixed, you paid for all the transportation costs."

In Bian Guanyue's eyes, Chen Guiliang was still dirt-poor, and she wanted to save him some money.

Chen Guiliang said mysteriously, "I'll tell you a secret. A big boss provided me with startup capital, and the plan to unearth the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor has taken another step forward. I have money now; I can still afford a cup of bubble tea."

"Would it kill you to not lie?" Bian Guanyue didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

"Fine, don't believe me." Chen Guiliang went off on his own to find a bubble tea shop.

Bian Guanyue quickly followed.

Without realizing it, she was already being led by Chen Guiliang.

As the saying goes, the person involved is confused, but the onlooker sees clearly.

Back when she was an onlooker to Chen Guiliang and Tao Xue's conversations, she could tell at a glance that Tao Xue was being led by the nose. Now that it was her turn, she was in a muddle, unable to figure things out.

And Chen Guiliang really did look better today.

Humans are, after all, visual creatures.

The bubble tea shop was very easy to find; you could see the throng of people from a long way off.

It was, after all, the only bubble tea shop in the entire county, and it hadn't been open for long. Many young people came to try it on the weekends, and the queue of customers was blocking the pedestrian street outside the shop.

"Whoa, so many people!" Chen Guiliang exclaimed in genuine amazement.

Bian Guanyue followed him to the end of the line. "Let's just forget it. We'll have to wait in line for a long time."

Chen Guiliang said, "There's a seating area over there. Why don't you go grab two seats first?"

"I'll wait in line with you."

As they spoke, Bian Guanyue looked around, afraid of running into any of her classmates.

Hanging out with a boy, queuing up to buy bubble tea, was an experience she'd never had before. She felt a strange sense of guilt, yet it was also very exciting.

While queuing, Bian Guanyue said, "The one thousand yuan I lent you for clothes, you don't have to be in a hurry to pay me back. You're actually very capable. You can get a work-study job when you get to university. I have a cousin who made a lot of money in university."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Did your cousin make money through a work-study program, or by starting her own business?"

Bian Guanyue said, "She's a business administration major. She started on Taobao during the SARS period, selling some of her old things. Later, she started sourcing her own goods, rented a place near the school as a warehouse, and specialized in selling electronic accessories like mobile phone chargers. The Samsung MP3 player I'm using now, I bought it from her Taobao store. It was actually her old second-hand one. By the way, do you know about Taobao?"

In 2003, when Taobao was just starting out, most sellers were selling second-hand goods. It was a lot like the later Xianyu platform.

Only after the SARS epidemic subsided did sellers of knock-off and no-name brand products become more common.

There were also sellers of genuine brand-name products, like Kodak film, which was quite popular. Because its production capacity had increased while its market size was shrinking, it resulted in a massive inventory backlog. Selling it at a low price on Taobao turned out to be extremely popular, and it shot up to become one of the top three best-selling items on the platform.

"I know it, Alibaba," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue was very surprised. "You actually know about Taobao? It's only popular in a few big cities."

Chen Guiliang put on an air. "Though I reside in a humble dwelling, my heart encompasses the world."

Bian Guanyue became more talkative. "My cousin advised me to get into a university in Hangcheng, so I can do Taobao with her. But I don't know anything about business, so I probably won't be much help."

"It's very simple. You're so smart, you'll definitely learn it in no time," Chen Guiliang said.

"But I don't want to do business," Bian Guanyue thought about it carefully. "Actually, I don't know what I want to do. I feel pretty lost."

Chen Guiliang coaxed her, "We can start a business together. That one thousand yuan for the clothes can be your share of the capital."

"No way, business is not easy," Bian Guanyue said.

The two chatted on and off. Bian Guanyue was in an excellent mood, much more cheerful than when they had first met.

After she transferred schools, she had gradually made some friends. Besides Chen Guiliang, there were Wang Siyu and Zheng Feng, as well as her new deskmate Wu Meng, and Tan Zhuo at the next table.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Are you getting along well with Wu Meng?"

Bian Guanyue smiled. "She's like me, usually doesn't talk much. But she's actually very warm-hearted. Every time I ask her for help with a difficult problem, she patiently explains it in detail. I actually know that those problems are extremely simple for her. It's because I'm too slow that she finds it hard to explain them clearly."

Chen Guiliang searched his memory and found that he knew almost nothing about Wu Meng.

He only knew that this top student had clinched the title of top liberal arts scholar in the city during the college entrance exams, and later heard that she had immigrated to Lee-Ka-Poh. But across two lifetimes, they had barely interacted, because Wu Meng had a very introverted personality and rarely spoke.

"She likes to eat fried mini potatoes. I buy some for her every day, and she often treats me to snacks in return." Bian Guanyue was getting more and more talkative now, proactively sharing details about her daily life with her new deskmate.

Chen Guiliang chimed in at the right moments, guiding her to continue, and Bian Guanyue chatted with even more enthusiasm.

The line moved forward little by little. By the time it was Chen Guiliang's turn, several dozen minutes had passed. "Two cups of pearl milk tea."

As he spoke, Chen Guiliang turned his head and asked Bian Guanyue, "What would you like to eat?"

This bubble tea shop was a bit unconventional; it also sold various pastries.

"Red bean cake," Bian Guanyue glanced at the menu board.

Chen Guiliang had the staff get the red bean cake, but he was complaining inwardly: The bubble tea is already sweet enough, and you're eating red bean cake on top of it. You'll get sick from the sweetness.

The two of them had stood in line until their legs were sore. Chen Guiliang carried the red bean cake and two cups of bubble tea, leading Bian Guanyue toward the casual dining area.

In this small county town, selling bubble tea was considered a high-end, fashionable business.

The shop even had a casual dining area set up to the side, filled with wrought-iron tables and chairs of a minimalist design. Sitting there drinking bubble tea felt just like eating steak in a Western restaurant.

It was all about the vibe!

The county town had no Western restaurants, no fast-food chains, and no cafes. The choices for fashionable teens were pitifully few.

Some young people even stayed after finishing their bubble tea, continuing to sit and enjoy the "petit bourgeois" lifestyle.

"Bian Guanyue, there are empty seats over here!"

In the seating area, Wang Siyu stood up and waved. Next to her was a girl he didn't recognize.

Running into Wang Siyu was a pleasant surprise for Bian Guanyue.

For some reason, she was suddenly afraid that Wang Siyu would misunderstand something, and immediately left Chen Guiliang to walk over by herself. "You're here for bubble tea too?"

Wang Siyu said, "I live in Fugui Gardens, just two bus stops from here. By the way, this is my junior high classmate, Yuan Wei. She's in the honors class for third-years at No. 1 High."

No. 1 High was the best school in the county, second only to No. 2 High.

Moreover, it had just moved to a new campus in the new district, and its facilities were better than No. 2 High's. The only downside was the landscaping; all the newly transplanted trees were bare.

"Weiwei, this is Bian Guanyue from my class."

"Hello."

"Hello."

Yuan Wei had delicate features and was quite pretty.

She proactively helped move a chair and said to Wang Siyu, "Xiao Yu, your classmate is so beautiful. Is she the school belle of No. 2 High?"

Wang Siyu said, "What school belle? You've been reading too many novels."

Bian Guanyue sat down with a smile, chatting briefly, and selectively forgetting about Chen Guiliang behind her.

In front of an acquaintance, she had to keep her distance from Chen Guiliang.

It hadn't been like this just a few days ago.

Could it be because Chen Guiliang had become handsome?

A girl's thoughts are hard to guess.

"Where's your bubble tea?" Wang Siyu asked.

Chen Guiliang lifted the bubble tea in his hand and said with a smile, "Classmate Wang Siyu, there's still a living person standing here."

Wang Siyu was stunned for a moment, then said in disbelief, "Chen Guiliang?"

Chen Guiliang sighed. "We sat one behind the other, you know. I can't believe you don't recognize me just because I changed my hairstyle. How heartbreaking."

"Holy crap!"

Wang Siyu had a very extroverted personality. She stood up and walked a circle around Chen Guiliang. "I never noticed before. So Hero Chen is actually a handsome guy."

After saying that, she added, "Really handsome, at least top three in our class. If I had known earlier, I would have pursued you myself. What a waste of a handsome resource."

"I've always been handsome, just in a more reserved way," Chen Guiliang pulled up a chair for himself and sat down, placing a cup of bubble tea in front of Bian Guanyue. "I'm not hiding it anymore today, I'm laying my cards on the table. If you regret not pursuing me, you still have a chance now."

Wang Siyu said scornfully, "Not only have you become handsome, you've also become a smooth talker."

"Woman, you are making excuses for your own lack of judgment," Chen Guiliang said with a straight face.

Wang Siyu couldn't be bothered with him and introduced him to her best friend, Yuan Wei. "This is my classmate, Chen Guiliang, whose nickname in the pugilistic world is Hero Chen. It's a miracle he hasn't been expelled for the things he's done at No. 2 High."

"Hello." Yuan Wei was much shier, especially when meeting a handsome guy. She spoke with a touch of bashfulness.

Chen Guiliang nodded in greeting. "Hello."

Wang Siyu completely ignored Chen Guiliang, flicking her hair and saying, "Bian Guanyue, look, I got an ion perm today too. My hair became so smooth and straight all of a sudden."

"Your hairstyle is beautiful, it really suits you," Bian Guanyue praised.

Chen Guiliang sipped his bubble tea through a straw, feeling a bit helpless inside. He had finally managed to coax a girl out, only to have two third wheels show up halfway.

The four of them sat down and started chatting. Wang Siyu talked about interesting things at No. 2 High, while Yuan Wei complained that No. 1 High was too strict.

The newly appointed principal of No. 1 High had implemented quasi-military management, and the students were finding it a bit hard to bear.

But the results were very obvious; No. 1 High's undergraduate acceptance rate had soared.

After finishing their bubble tea, they continued to chat.

But the young people nearby who didn't have seats would come over to hurry them along from time to time, forcing Chen Guiliang's group of four to give up their spot.

Wang Siyu looked at her watch and said, "It's almost noon, let's go get something to eat."

Bian Guanyue politely declined, "I told my grandpa and grandma I'd be back for lunch."

"Then let's hang out next time," Wang Siyu said.

"Okay!"

"Goodbye!"

The four of them waved to each other.

Chen Guiliang accompanied Bian Guanyue to the roadside to wait for the bus.

Wang Siyu and Yuan Wei lived in Fugui Gardens, and could stroll home in just two bus stops' distance.

Once they were farther away, Yuan Wei asked, "Are those two classmates of yours dating?"

"Not sure," Wang Siyu thought carefully. "Something is definitely a bit off. They used to listen to music together, and today they came out for bubble tea. And, and, Chen Guiliang is wearing new clothes and got a new hairstyle. There's definitely something fishy going on!"

Yuan Wei said, "I think they look good together."

"You don't know," Wang Siyu said. "Chen Guiliang has always been really poor. I've hardly ever seen him in new clothes. He had a pair of pants in his second year of high school, and because he grew taller, they didn't even cover his ankles by his third year, but he kept wearing them. I felt sorry for him. Bian Guanyue's family is really rich. Her phone, MP3 player, and laptop are all brand-name!"

Yuan Wei smiled and said, "You're too materialistic. Love is about mutual affection, it has nothing to do with worldly possessions."

Wang Siyu suddenly thought of Zheng Feng and said with schadenfreude, "I don't know if I'm materialistic, but someone might be about to go crazy. Hero Chen is truly amazing, snatching up the beauty in one fell swoop!"

After seeing Bian Guanyue home, Chen Guiliang, carrying several shopping bags, went straight to a nearby internet cafe.

He carefully read the replies from netizens, felt that the time was about right, and sent a QQ message to Yang Yuhui: "Brother Yang, we're moving into phase three this afternoon."

"Roger!" Yang Yuhui replied instantly.

The shills were activated.

Shill No. 1 posted a thread suggesting that this private server should have memberships. Those willing to pay to show support could become members, while those unwilling could just be part of the community. Members wouldn't have any special privileges, but they could use an accelerator for a smoother gaming experience on the private server.

Selling accelerators was also one of the ways private servers made money at the time.

Shill No. 2 immediately replied, saying that this private server was about dreams and youth, and once it became monetized, it would lose its purity.

The two shills quickly started flaming each other.

Shill No. 3, 4, 5, 6… gradually joined the discussion, intentionally steering the direction of public opinion.

More and more netizens were drawn into the thread, launching a debate over whether the server should be monetized.

Gradually, the side supporting monetization gained the upper hand, with the reasoning that the dream-chaser shouldn't have to lose money. However, they absolutely could not sell gear, otherwise the game would be meaningless.

That fellow from Beijing named Fu Guoqiang, who followed the related posts every day, directly replied with a comment: "If the private server doesn't sell gear and maintains the purity of the game, I'm willing to sponsor 5,000 yuan for free!"

And there was more than one rich person. Soon, someone else replied: "I'll sponsor 300 yuan."

"I'm an office worker, I'll sponsor 50 yuan as a small token."

"I can sponsor 10 yuan. You won't think it's too little, right?"

"It's not too little, even 1 yuan is fine. Many hands make light work!"

"..."

Yang Yuhui used the account "A Sword from the West" to post a thread: "Regarding the matter of sponsorship, I appreciate everyone's kind intentions, but only accepting sponsorship fees is not a long-term solution. My friends and I discussed it until midnight last night and have roughly come up with a way to recover our costs. I can't disclose the specifics just yet. But I solemnly promise not to sell gear, not to sell memberships, not to sell cheats, and not to sell accelerators!"

This statement was very mysterious, leading to even more speculation and discussion among the netizens.

The threads about whether to charge, and how to charge, received more and more replies, developing in the direction Chen Guiliang had preset.

Chen Guiliang's intention, of course, was to lay the groundwork for selling admission tickets.

It was a preemptive measure!

He was giving the players a mental heads-up, lest selling tickets suddenly upon the server's launch would easily provoke players' resentment and anger.

Our slogan is:

To ensure that every player can enjoy all in-game services for free, we are committed to creating a truly free game.
